- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–2% to capture momentum.
- In low-news periods (news volume ≤1.0), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for reduced volatility.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overcorrects; apply a 1–2% downward bias to align with mean reversion.
